16.text: The inner trousers are made of soft fawn-

17.text: skins of varying thickness, according to the

18.text: season. The Chukchee trousers have no regular

19.text: belt and are short in the waist, scarcely reaching

20.text: the navel (see Fig. 170). They are held in

21.text: place by a sinew string which passes through

22.text: a hem at their upper edge. Notwithstanding

23.text: this, they always have a tendency to slip down.

24.text: The Chukchee men habitually give a peculiar

25.text: jerk to their bodies to throw the trousers back

26.text: to the proper place. The trousers are narrow,

27.text: and fit the calf of the leg tightly. On the

28.text: lower edge they have the usual gathering-string,

29.text: which can be drawn tight around the ankle.

30.text: The short legs of the Chukchee boots are always put inside the trousers, so

31.text: that, when the latter are tied, the whole is impervious to snow.

32.text: Trousers of seal-skin are worn in spring and in summer by the Maritime

33.text: people, and by reindeer-breeders who live near the coast. Their cut is exactly

34.text: the same as that of the trousers of reindeer-skin, and they are often adorned

35.text: their full length with narrow stripes dyed purple. Those worn by young men

36.text: often have numerous tassels of the skin of a seal-pup dyed red¹ (Fig. 170).

37.text: Trousers with many tassels indicate the claim of their owner to a wrestling

38.text: reputation, from which fact they are called “wrestler’s trousers.” Wealthy people

39.text: sometimes have dress trousers, likewise tasselled, and made of the skin of fur-

40.text: seal, which is extremely rare on these shores.
